sections.html:
Keizer is a Marion County city in the Willamette Valley, about 3 miles north of downtown Salem and 43 miles south of Portland. Salem borders it on the south and east, and the Willamette River forms its southwestern edge, separating it from Polk County. The city measures 7.36 square miles, and its ZIP codes are 97303 and 97307.

The 2020 census counted 39,376 people, up from 36,478 in 2010, and the estimate for July 1, 2025 is 39,140. There were 14,706 households in 2020, 60.6 percent of them owner-occupied, and the median age was 38.0.

Voters incorporated Keizer on November 2, 1982, on the seventh try, by 4,440 to 3,341. Rapid residential growth in the 1990s means many houses are now about three decades old, and some are older still.

Parts of Keizer sit in the Willamette River floodplain, and buyers expect flood history to come up. Floods struck in 1861, 1943, 1945, 1946 and 1948, and dams built in the 1950s helped regulate the river. The February 1996 flood damaged several homes, and some residents received FEMA funds to move out of the floodplain.

A private flood-risk model estimates that about 3,060 Keizer properties, 53 percent of the city, face a greater than 26 percent chance of severe flood impact over 30 years. Treat that as background, not a verdict on any single lot, and check the official maps for your address. Areas often named as sensitive to high water include Claggett Creek, Chemawa Road NE, Keizer Rapids Park and Spong's Landing.

The city has a floodplain overlay zone in its code, and Marion County runs a floodplain program. Before you list, find out whether your lot is mapped and whether you carry flood insurance. A buyer's lender will ask, and documented answers keep a deal moving.

Keizer shares the Salem-area climate, with warm dry summers and a wet, cool season from October through April. July highs average about 83.5 degrees, annual precipitation is about 40 inches and snow averages roughly 3.5 inches. The record high is 117 degrees and the record low is minus 12.

Months of steady rain test roofs, gutters and crawl spaces every year. With much of the housing dating from the 1990s growth period, roofs, windows and systems are reaching replacement age, and sellers who skipped upkeep tend to hear about it in inspections.

sections.h2: Roads, schools and getting to work
sections.html:
Interstate 5 runs along the northeast border of Keizer, with access at Exit 260A on Chemawa Road NE, and Oregon Route 99E runs just outside the southeastern limit. Most residents work elsewhere, and the largest nearby employers are in Salem, including the State of Oregon and Salem Hospital.

Keizer belongs to the Salem-Keizer School District. The city has one high school, McNary, plus Claggett Creek and Whiteaker middle schools and seven elementary schools: Clear Lake, Cummings, Forest Ridge, Gubser, Keizer, Kennedy and Weddle. Check which one serves your address before you advertise it.

Keizer calls itself the Iris Capital of the World and holds KeizerFEST, the Iris Festival, each May. The city maintains 18 parks covering more than 200 acres. Keizer Rapids Park has river frontage, trails, a dog park and an amphitheater, and Keizer Stadium, which opened in 1997, hosts the Salem-Keizer Volcanoes. A short mention of nearby parks and festivals in your listing tells a buyer things a photo cannot, and the school buildings nearby, including the 1916 building that now holds the Keizer Heritage Community Center and Museum, add local character.

Marion County mails statements between October 15 and 25. Choose how to pay:

Payment optionDue dateDiscount
Full amountNovember 153 percent
Two-thirdsNovember 15, with the last third due May 152 percent
One-third installmentsNovember 15, February 15, May 15None

Mailed payments must be postmarked by November 15.

If your statement has not arrived by November 1, call the Tax Department at (503) 588-5215. The county applies a payment to the oldest tax year with a balance first, which matters if a past year is unpaid on a house you plan to sell. Details are on the Marion County payment information page. Your title company will prorate the current year at closing.

sections.h2: Paperwork to gather before you list
sections.html:
A tidy folder lets you answer buyer questions the same day. For a Keizer house, start with the items below.

  • Your current tax statement, plus proof that earlier years are paid.
  • Any flood insurance policy, elevation certificate or FEMA map printout for your lot.
  • Receipts for roof, window, plumbing or electrical work done since you bought.
  • The mortgage payoff figure from your lender.
  • Probate or trust papers if the house is part of an estate.

Because the county applies payments to the oldest year first, check that no old balance is sitting on the account. Clearing it before you list avoids a delay when the title company runs its search.

After you accept an offer, a title company opens escrow, searches the property for liens and unpaid taxes, and prepares the closing documents. The tax for the current year is divided between you and the buyer, your mortgage is paid off from the proceeds, and the deed is recorded with the county.

If a flood question or a roof problem surfaces during the buyer's inspection, you can fix it, lower the price or let the buyer take the house as it is. Decide your limit before negotiations begin, so a surprise does not stall the closing.

The city's plan says Keizer lacks enough land for the housing it needs, and an urban growth boundary limits expansion. Developers are using state law to build clusters of up to four homes on lots once zoned for one. If you own a larger lot, a buyer may value it for that reason, so ask the city about what the zoning allows before you set a price.

• Flood questions: buyers and lenders ask about mapping and insurance.
  • Aging houses: homes from the 1990s growth period can need new roofs, windows and systems.
  • Limited land: few new lots means resale houses carry more weight.
  • Small-lot infill: new clusters of homes can compete with resales.

If you want to avoid repairs, showings and a lender's appraisal, ask a cash buyer for terms in writing and compare them with a listing. A title company handles closing in either case, so liens, tax proration and the deed work the same way.

We buy houses in Keizer as they are, including houses with flood questions or aging systems. Request an offer online or by phone, and gather your tax statement, mortgage payoff figure and any flood insurance papers to speed the process.

faqs.q: What county is Keizer, Oregon in?
faqs.a: Keizer is in Marion County, just north of Salem. The Willamette River separates it from Polk County to the southwest.
Voters incorporated Keizer on November 2, 1982, on the seventh attempt, by 4,440 to 3,341.

faqs.q: Is Keizer in a flood zone?
faqs.a: Parts of Keizer are in the Willamette River floodplain. The city has a floodplain overlay zone, and floods hit in 1861, the 1940s and February 1996. Check official maps for your specific address.

faqs.q: How many people live in Keizer?
faqs.a: The estimate for July 1, 2025 is 39,140 residents. The 2020 census counted 39,376.

faqs.q: When are Marion County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first payment is due November 15, with a 3 percent discount for paying in full. Remaining installments fall on February 15 and May 15.
